jobs.prompt:
FILE ACCESS: declared outputs are writable. Tests first. Harden the owner-only gate for `swarm tickets supersede` and `tickets --set superseded` in tools/scope-commands.mjs (supersedeOwnerRefusal ~line 3449). The review's exploit: any agent can export SWARM_OWNER=1, or allocate a pty, and get through, because the gate trusts an env string and isTTY.

New rules:
1) Remove the SWARM_OWNER=1 production bypass entirely. No environment string makes an agent session the owner.
2) Agent/worker markers always refuse, checked first: CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT, SWARM_WORKER, SWARM_JOB_ID, SWARM_RUN_ID (present today; keep them).
3) Add process-ancestry detection: walk the parent process chain from this process (default: `ps -o ppid= -p <pid>` and `ps -o comm= -p <pid>`, up to 32 hops, stop at pid 1) and refuse if any ancestor's command basename (lowercased) is a known agent: claude, codex, cursor-agent, opencode, chatgpt. This closes the pty trick: a pty created inside an agent still has the agent in its ancestry. Keep the helper injectable (`ancestry` array or a `processInfo` dep) for tests.
4) Still require isTTY (both stdin and stdout) after the ancestry/marker checks.
5) Keep one test-only seam so the existing success-path command tests can run without a real owner terminal: a module-scoped `setSupersedeOwnerCheck(fn)` / reset hook used by both the bulk command and the `--set superseded` path (production always calls the real gate; the hook is for tests only, no env bypass). Tests must reset it.

Update tests/tickets-supersede.test.mjs: SWARM_OWNER=1 with an agent marker still refuses; isTTY true with ancestry ['bash','codex'] refuses; isTTY true with clean ancestry allows; no TTY refuses; the bulk command and `--set superseded` both refuse through the real gate and allow through the test hook. Keep every other test. Verify: node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/tickets-supersede.test.mjs tests/scope-commands.test.mjs tests/tickets.test.mjs -> all pass. Report counts.
